title: Macro Defect Inspection - Pattern Defects Detection on ATL/LMS IPRO8
subtitle: Post-Etch Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the ATL/LMS IPRO8 system to detect and classify Pattern Defects defects during post-etch inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Pattern Defects defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the ATL/LMS IPRO8 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: ATL/LMS IPRO8
- Inspection Type: Macro Defect Inspection
- Target Defect: Pattern Defects
- Process Step: Post-Etch
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all ATL/LMS IPRO8 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-etch monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: ATL/LMS IPRO8
Software Version: v10.8.243
Recipe: MACRO_DEFECT_INSPECTION_45nm_POST_ETCH
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (117 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the ATL/LMS IPRO8 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Macro Defect Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Pattern Defects defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 64 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.6% for Macro Defect Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-10-28
Wafers Tested: 19
Total Defects Found: 2794
Defect Density: 889.36 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.8%
Capture Rate: 95.8%
Test Duration: 426 minutes
System Uptime: 96.2%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The ATL/LMS IPRO8 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Pattern Defects at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Pattern Defects at 45nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
